blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built from provincial and municipal pages named under Sources, read November 1, 2026.
These BC rules apply to every condo purchase on this site, whichever neighbourhood it is in. They are written once here; each community page covers only what is specific to that community.
Rental-restriction bylaws are void

Since November 24, 2022, strata bylaws anywhere in BC can't ban or limit long-term rentals, so a "rentals not allowed" line in a listing or building directory doesn't apply to long-term rentals. Short-term rentals are different: stratas can still ban or limit them by bylaw, local zoning may restrict them, and a provincial short-term rental registration number has been required since May 1, 2025. Age bylaws: only a 55-and-older bylaw is allowed, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and (since May 1, 2023) younger spouses or partners and some children.
Presales (REDMA)
a presale buyer has seven days to cancel, from the later of signing and acknowledging the disclosure statement, and deposits are held in trust.
Property Transfer Tax (BC)

1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million and 3% above $2 million, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million; a purchase under $2 million pays only the 1% and 2% rates. The newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and partial up to $1,150,000.
Depreciation reports

Since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get one every five years and can't vote to skip it, and since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the operating budget must go into the contingency reserve. An older building with a pool, hot tub or recreation centre carries roof, building envelope and amenity costs that show up in its fees, so read the depreciation report before comparing its fees with a newer or simpler building's.
Form B

The Form B shows a strata lot's monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. The strata paperwork is where a strata home's real cost shows up: the Province's guidance points buyers to the Form B, the Form F, the bylaws and rules, fees and special levies, and that's where age, pet and rental rules are, not in the listing.
Federal savings vehicles

Home Buyers' Plan: $60,000 per buyer from RRSPs. First Home Savings Account: $8,000 a year, up to $40,000. Mortgage default insurance (CMHC): premiums run 0.6% to 4.5%, plus 0.2% where the over-25-year amortization surcharge applies.
Mortgage default insurance (CMHC)

Premiums run from 0.6% (borrowing up to 65% of the price) to 4.0% (90.01% to 95%), or 4.5% at the top with a non-traditional down payment, plus 0.2% where the over-25-year amortization surcharge applies.
GST on new condos

5% GST applies to new construction, not resales. Moody on the Hill was built in 2024, so whether GST is payable depends on the specific home's sale history (a first sale from the developer or a resale). The First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate rebates 100% of the GST on a price up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out by $1.5 million, for agreements signed on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031. The legislation (Bill C-4) received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026, according to the Canada Revenue Agency. The older GST New Housing Rebate (36%, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000) still exists.
55+ bylaws
Only a 55+ age bylaw is legal, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, a live-in caregiver, existing residents and some children (expanded May 1, 2023).
GST and rebates

5% GST applies to new construction, not resales. A never-occupied home in a tower finished in 2025 (Plaza One, Plaza Two, The Grand on King George, Park George) can still be a sale by the developer, so find out for each home whether it's a developer sale or a resale. The First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, according to the Canada Revenue Agency) rebates 100% of the GST up to $1 million, to a maximum of $50,000, phasing out by $1.5 million, for agreements signed from March 20, 2025 and before 2031. The GST New Housing Rebate is 36%, to a maximum of $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.
Depreciation reports and CRF

since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, no deferral by vote; and since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF.
Minimum CRF contribution
effective November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the contingency reserve fund in the annual budget.
55+ is the only legal age bylaw

Only a 55+ age bylaw is legal, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and some children. That works two ways in this city: the Fraserview Village buildings are published as 55+ (confirm the registered bylaw with the Form B), while Canuck Plaza's "25+" label is void, because no age other than 55+ can be a legal strata age bylaw. Haney Pioneer Village is a 60+ co-op, and its age rule is a co-op rule, not a strata bylaw.

faq.a: Pet bylaws can still be enforced in BC, unlike rental bans, so check the registered bylaws in the Form B package for the specific building. Listing lines such as "pets allowed" or "cats OK" aren't the bylaws.

Property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. For example, a $560,000 condo with no exemption pays $9,200 ($2,000 + $7,200).

In an ordinary resale, yes: the strata must provide a Form B within 7 days of a proper request. In a court-ordered sale, read the conditions of sale line by line with a lawyer, and allow for anything you may not get.
faq.q: Will I get the full strata documents — Form B, minutes, depreciation report?

faq.a: No. BC government and BCFSA consumer guidance doesn't require open house visitors to sign in or show ID.
faq.q: Do I have to sign in or show ID at an open house?

faq.a: Yes, two ways the rules themselves create: the person with conduct may apply to confirm a sale even before the redemption period expires (Rule 21-7(9)), but until the confirming order is made the sale is not final; and the court's directions may define rights to bid, make offers or meet bids (Rule 13-5(4)(d)), so a competing bid at the approval stage is a real possibility in this process.
faq.q: Can my accepted offer still lose?

faq.a: That is what the confirming order does: on the Rule 21-7(9) application the court may order the sale confirmed, direct the disposition of the proceeds and vest title in the purchaser; the result of the sale is certified in Form 60 (Rule 13-5(6)). The vesting order, not the listing, is the title-cleaning step.
faq.q: Is the title clean if I win?

faq.a: The strata package behind the Form B: the depreciation report (required every five years for stratas with 5 or more lots since July 1, 2024), financial statements, the contingency reserve balance and planned work, which BCREA advises reviewing to spot future special levies. In an older building, that package matters more than the staging.
